say.en: In the monsoon, the paddy fields of Karnataka echo with frog calls. Only the males call. How else can we tell a male frog from a female? In this lesson: Describe the habits of the frog.
Describe its external features.
State the signs of sexual dimorphism.

body.en: The common Indian frog is Rana tigrina. Frogs are cold-blooded (poikilotherms): their body temperature changes with the environment. They can change colour to hide from enemies, which is camouflage. To escape the heat of summer and the cold of winter they shelter in deep burrows; this is aestivation and hibernation. A frog never drinks water but absorbs it through its skin.
body.kn: ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಕಪ್ಪೆ ರಾನಾ ಟೈಗ್ರಿನಾ. ಕಪ್ಪೆ ಶೀತರಕ್ತ ಪ್ರಾಣಿ; ಬಣ್ಣ ಬದಲಿಸಿ ಅಡಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಬೇಸಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗ್ರೀಷ್ಮನಿದ್ರೆ, ಚಳಿಗಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಶಿಶಿರನಿದ್ರೆ. ಕಪ್ಪೆ ನೀರು ಕುಡಿಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಚರ್ಮದ ಮೂಲಕ ಹೀರುತ್ತದೆ.

explanation.en: The frog's body has a head and a trunk; there is no neck or tail. The eyes bulge and are covered by a nictitating membrane in water; the tympanum (ear) receives sound. Hind limbs are larger and webbed for swimming. Males have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of each forelimb.

say.en: Rana tigrina, the common Indian frog. Name its external parts.

body.en: The skin is smooth and slippery because of mucus. The dorsal side is olive green with dark irregular spots and the ventral side is pale yellow. The body is divided into a head and a trunk; there is no neck or tail. Above the mouth are a pair of nostrils. The bulging eyes are covered by a nictitating membrane that protects them in water, and a membranous tympanum on each side receives sound. Forelimbs end in four digits and the larger, muscular hindlimbs in five webbed digits that help in swimming.
body.kn: ಕಪ್ಪೆಯ ಚರ್ಮ ಲೋಳೆಯಿಂದ ನುಣುಪು. ದೇಹ ತಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ಮುಂಡ; ಕುತ್ತಿಗೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬಾಲ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಕಣ್ಣುಗಳನ್ನು ನಿಕ್ಟಿಟೇಟಿಂಗ್ ಪೊರೆ ರಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಕಿವಿಯಾಗಿ ಟಿಂಪನಮ್. ಮುಂಗಾಲಿಗೆ ನಾಲ್ಕು, ಹಿಂಗಾಲಿಗೆ ಐದು ಬೆರಳುಗಳು.

myth.en: Frogs drink water through the mouth like other land animals.

truth.en: Frogs never drink water; they absorb it through their moist, permeable skin. We assume all thirsty animals drink. Frog skin is thin, moist and richly supplied with blood, so it absorbs water and also exchanges gases.

say.en: Rana tigrina: poikilotherm; aestivation (summer) and hibernation (winter); never drinks water.
No neck or tail; nictitating membrane; tympanum; 4 digits on forelimb, 5 webbed on hind limb. Males: vocal sacs and copulatory pads.
Three-chambered heart, sinus venosus, conus arteriosus; hepatic and renal portal systems; nucleated RBCs.
Ureotelic; male ureters are urinogenital ducts; 10 pairs of cranial nerves.
External fertilisation; 2500–3000 ova; tadpole larva with metamorphosis.

problem.en: A student is given two frogs. One has swellings at the throat and a rough pad on the first finger of each forelimb. State the sex of each frog with reasons.

steps.en: Vocal sacs (throat swellings) are found only in males.
A copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimb is also a male feature.
So the frog with these features is male; the other, lacking them, is female.

answer.en: First frog male (vocal sacs, copulatory pad); second female
